title: AUTISM AND NEURODIVERSITY
description: Examines autism and neurodiversity from a psychological perspective. Emphasizes the scientific basis of autism and neurodiversity, with an emphasis on research co-created with autistic researchers and reflecting the lived experience of autistic and neurodivergent individuals, including those with a range of support needs, in social context. Critically examines historical and current diagnostic criteria and processes, evidence-based therapies, interventions and supports, and inclusive workplace, educational, legal, and healthcare environments that allow autistic and neurodivergent people to enjoy fulfilling, interdependent lives in community with other neurotypical and neurodivergent people.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: (PSY 201Z, 201HZ, 201 or 201H) and (PSY 202Z, 202HZ, 202 or 202H).
A minimum grade of C- is required in PSY 201Z, PSY 201HZ, PSY 201, PSY 201H, PSY 202Z, PSY 202HZ, PSY 202 and PSY 202H.

Students with a term class standing of Freshman or Sophomore may not enroll.
